input.question: Why is orange juice much cheaper than oranges?
input.ground_truth: Aside from the fact that juice manufacturers can buy in maybe bulk, thereby getting discounts, and aside from the fact that through futures (contracts that guarantee specified supply of oranges at a set price, irrespective of supply and demand spikes), oranges that you buy at the site are not the same as oranges for juicing. Store oranges are bred with size, color and hardiness in mind, whereas juicing oranges are bred for moisture content alone. Those moisture content oranges are cheaper to produce, and are produced at much greater quantities, altogether, this keeps the price low.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Why is orange juice much cheaper than oranges?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a big orange tree. If you want to drink orange juice, you have to pick the oranges, squeeze them, and throw away the peels and seeds. So, you don’t get to keep all the orange—you only get the juice.

But if you want to eat an orange, you can just take it and eat the whole thing (except maybe the peel). So, making juice from oranges uses up more oranges and makes some parts go to waste.

Also, people buy a lot of orange juice, and it’s easy to sell in big containers. That’s why orange juice can be cheaper than buying a bunch of oranges. Plus, sometimes, juice is made from oranges that aren’t perfect to eat, so they’re cheaper to buy.
